levels.title: Your first commit
levels.briefing: A commit is a snapshot of your project at a moment in time. You choose what goes into the snapshot by staging files with git add, then save it with git commit.
levels.objective: Create a file called notes.txt with any text in it, then commit it.

cheatsheet.description: Stage a file for the next commit

hints: First the file has to exist. You can create it in the terminal or with the file editor.
Once notes.txt exists, stage it, then commit it with a message.
Run: echo "my notes" > notes.txt, then git add notes.txt, then git commit -m "Add notes"
levels.successMessage: You staged notes.txt and saved it in a new commit. That commit is now part of your project history, which you can see in the graph.

levels.title: Commit two files at once
levels.objective: Create todo.txt and ideas.txt, then save both in a single new commit.
hints: A single commit can contain several files. Stage both before you commit.
Create both files, add both, then commit once.
Run: touch todo.txt ideas.txt, then git add todo.txt ideas.txt, then git commit -m "Add lists"
levels.successMessage: Both files went into one commit, because a commit saves everything that is staged at that moment.
